title: Document the engine installer and version contract
summary: The engine repository's README and CHANGELOG describe the one-command engine installer, the launcher and PATH behaviour, uninstall, the machine-readable version, and how the version a configured source or ref provides is obtained and compared.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

result.summary: Documented the engine installer and version contract in the user-facing introduction, the detailed install guide, and the release notes, consistent with the shipped installer and the shipped version report. README's Install section is now the first thing a user reads: prerequisites (checkout plus Python 3.11 or newer on PATH), the single step `sh install.sh`, where the engine and the `forgel` entry point land (`~/.local/share/forgel`, `~/.local/bin/forgel`, or the `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT`/`FORGEL_BIN_DIR` overrides), the delimited start-up block that puts the command directory ahead on PATH, starting a new terminal session, and what to do when the name is still unreachable in the user's own shell. It states how the install is confirmed with the engine's `version --json` report, that the report is one JSON object a program consumes directly as the supported compatibility judgement and needs no project, model credential or particular working directory, that `sh install.sh --resolve` determines the version a configured source and reference would provide before anything is installed and that this value is what an installed engine is compared against, that only a strictly newer available version replaces an installed engine while an equal or older one leaves it untouched, and what `--uninstall` removes and which configuration and project material under `~/.forgel` it keeps. docs/install.md was brought in line with the same shipped behaviour: prerequisites and the single step, a new section on placement, shell reachability and the remedy for an unreachable location, a new section on confirming the install and the directly consumable report, the pre-install determination and the strictly-newer comparison rule, and removal rewritten to name the engine tree, the entry point, the start-up block and the kept user data. CHANGELOG.md gains entries for the single install step with entry point and shell reachability, pre-install version determination, the comparison rule, removal that keeps user data, and the directly consumable version report. No installer, entry point, version-reporting or removal behaviour was changed, no release version or tag was named, and no test, guard or assertion inspecting documentation was added. Verified by running the repository gate, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, which passed (820 tests), plus the installer and version suites specifically; every documented name, option, default location and output shape was read from install.sh, src/forgel/engine_version.py, src/forgel/entry.py and tests/test_install.py.

assumptions: The existing documentation task was continued rather than restarted: the installer, entry point, uninstall path and pre-install version determination are now shipped by install.sh on this branch, so the guidance describes that shipped behaviour instead of the earlier blocked state.

The strictly-newer comparison is documented as the rule the caller driving the installer applies (the engine installer installs the target it resolved), matching the shipped installer, which offers `--resolve` for the available version and no downgrade check of its own.

Removal is documented as removing the engine tree, the entry point and the installer's start-up block while keeping the user's configuration and project material under `~/.forgel`, which is what the shipped uninstall does.
Documentation was verified by reading it against the shipped installer and version report only; per the repository rules no automated check that reads documentation was added.
result.last_summary: stopped by the controller: The documentation task is sound but has an unmet prerequisite that this task cannot create. The failure is not a specification defect (the spec explicitly requires documenting only shipped behaviour), not a repository test or environment problem, and not a limit; the earlier decisions — respec, retry, two reworks, restart, QA, and a raised limit — have all exhausted the space of re-runs, and each returned the same fact: the engine has no installer, entry point on PATH, profile/reachability handling, uninstall path, or pre-install version determination. The only shipped piece is the version inquiry, so FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-5, FR-6, FR-7 and their acceptance criteria cannot be met truthfully, and writing them anyway would break FR-8/AC-8. The plan's backlog item 2, which must implement the installer, is itself marked blocked (dependency scout exceeded its step limit), and the escalated install.sh/test_install.py from an earlier attempt were never committed. Re-running this task unchanged reproduces the same conclusion; no runtime next-step operation can retarget the prerequisite task from here. The work must stop with this reason so the plan sequencing is corrected: unblock and implement the engine installer task, then re-queue this documentation task against the shipped behaviour.
